bullets.title: NVDA: Beat/raise with FY28 guidance to +75% but overwhelmed by CEO turmoil, SEC probe, and China chip halt
bullets.body: NVDA reported Q3 revenue of $115.8B (+103% YoY, beat consensus $109B) and guided Q4 to $130B; FY28 revenue growth raised to ~75% from ~70%. However, the board ruled out reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, an SEC civil probe into potential accounting issues opened, and NVDA halted Hopper/H200 shipments to China (~$2.4B in Q3 revenue). Multiple analysts cut PTs: Jefferies to $250 (Blayne Curtis), UBS to $220-$240, Piper to $230, Wolfe to $200—all maintaining Buy but citing CEO succession risk, 2028 visibility gap, and BIS export control headwinds. Stock down ~47% from ATH by week-end.

bullets.title: NVDA/AI chips: BIS interim rule tightens remote access to US compute; TSMC/Samsung halt China shipments
bullets.body: Commerce issued an interim final rule requiring export licenses for advanced AI chip sales to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil; overseas data centers renting compute to Chinese firms now need licenses. TSMC and Samsung suspended chip shipments to Chinese customers pending compliance. BIS estimates 1-2 GW of AI chip demand eliminated, impacting NVDA most. AMD fell 8% separately on a Hunterbrook short report alleging China server exposure via IEIT Systems.

bullets.title: INTU: FQ1 beat but Credit Karma guidance slashed; sells Mailchimp; stock -10%
bullets.body: INTU reported FQ1 revenue of $4.35B (+12% YoY, 1.2% beat) and EPS of $2.91 (+18.3% beat), but cut FY27 Credit Karma growth to 3-7% from 11-13% citing higher rates and AI-powered discovery shifts (consumers bypassing CK to find products directly via AI). FY27 consolidated revenue guidance lowered to 8-9% from 9-10%. Mailchimp sold to Bending Spoons for $3.68B. Multiple banks cut PTs: Mizuho to $380 (Outperform), KeyBanc to $375 (OW), UBS to $315 (Neutral). Stock trades at 9x NTM FCF.

bullets.title: BILL: TPG/Corpay take-private at $63.25/share; BILL downgraded across Wall Street
bullets.body: BILL agreed to be acquired by TPG (majority) and Corpay (minority, ~$1.1B for ~1/3 stake with option to buy remainder in 2030) at $63.25/share in cash, valuing the company at ~$6.0B (~4.2x NTM revenue). The 31% premium to 60-day VWAP caps upside; Mizuho raises PT to match deal price at $63.25 and maintains Neutral. JPMorgan, UBS, Jefferies, TD Cowen, Needham, Wolfe all downgraded to Neutral/Hold. Deal expected to close 1H27.

bullets.title: DIS: F4Q26 strong beat; FY27 double-digit EPS growth guidance; dividend raised 33%
bullets.body: Disney reported F4Q26 EPS of $1.77 (beat $1.67 consensus) and revenue of $25.95B (beat $25.16B). Management reaffirmed double-digit FY27 adjusted EPS growth; raised annual dividend 33% to $2.00/share; planning ~$9B share repurchases and ~$11B FCF in FY27. Domestic parks attendance +11%; SVOD OI margins 13.6% vs 7.9% year-ago. Citi maintains Buy at $140 PT; UBS raises to Buy; JPM reiterates OW.

bullets.title: TTWO: GTA VI launch—99 Metacritic, $3.79B day-one retail sales, record Twitch viewership
bullets.body: Take-Two's GTA VI launched with a 99 Metacritic score (tied all-time high), $3.79B in day-one retail sales, 32.5M presold units, and 3.31M concurrent Twitch viewers (5.5x the prior record for any game). UBS maintains Buy; every 10M unit upside = ~$600M vs. $8.0-8.2B bookings guidance. Stock up ~$5.72 on the day.

bullets.title: CRWD/ZS: CrowdStrike said to be in acquisition talks with Zscaler; ZS +18% AH
bullets.body: Bloomberg and wire services reported CrowdStrike is in acquisition talks with Zscaler. ZS surged 18% in after-hours trading on the news; no deal terms disclosed.

bullets.title: ORCL: Secures all OpenAI funding; targets >$30B FCF in FY29 and >$225B revenue in FY30
bullets.body: Oracle confirmed it has secured all funding needed for its OpenAI contract, completing $10B equity and $10B debt raises. Abilene (Astra-6 training site) is nearly complete; Shackelford GW-scale campus fully permitted; Vera Rubin rack handover on track. FY27 revenue guided >$90B (>34% YoY cc); FY30 targeting >$225B at 35%+ CAGR. Positive FCF expected H2 FY28, targeting self-funding from FY29.

bullets.title: DLR/data center REITs down 8-9% on AI policy headwinds; Trump bans overseas data center builds
bullets.body: Data center REITs fell ~8.75% for the week. DLR specifically dropped 9.73% on SE Asia regional concerns from BIS remote-access restrictions and Trump's announced policy taxing US companies building data centers abroad. Loudoun County VA passed a 12-month moratorium; Texas governor-elect Hinojosa plans permit freeze; North Carolina governor called for repealing data center tax incentives. BXDC's $5B Amazon sale-leaseback at 7% cap rate was a bright spot.

bullets.title: GOOGL: JPM reiterates OW at $375 PT on Gemini model cadence; YouTube facing $3B school settlement
bullets.body: JPM reiterates Overweight on Alphabet at $375 Dec-27 PT citing three new Gemini 4 models in under a month (Neon ranked #3 on Artificial Analysis Index), Gemini Tasks rollout to 1B+ users, and Cloud at +103% YoY with $561B backlog. Separately, YouTube is finalizing a ~$3B settlement with schools over social media addiction claims (a prior jury found Google 30% liable vs Meta 70%).

bullets.title: AVGO: Google cutting 2027 Broadcom TPU 8i shipments ~20%, shifting to MediaTek design
bullets.body: Per Ming-Chi Kuo, Google is cutting 2027 Broadcom-designed TPU 8i series shipments by ~1M units (~20%), primarily the higher-priced 8i Max/Whalefish models, and increasing MediaTek-designed TPU 8t shipments. Shift driven by frontier model development priority and power/supply chain constraints. Negative read-through for AVGO's custom silicon revenue in 2027.

bullets.title: MDB: UBS upgrades to Buy, PT to $450 from $375 (47% upside)
bullets.body: UBS upgraded MongoDB from Neutral to Buy, raising the price target to $450 from $375 citing durable 20%+ total revenue growth and 25%+ Atlas growth. The upgrade comes despite a recent CEO departure; UBS sees management turnover as a sentiment clearing event rather than fundamental change.

bullets.title: SPOT: CFO at TMT conf signals mid-teens revenue growth through 2030; AI Remix near Q1 launch
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains Overweight on Spotify at $700 PT (~30x FY28 FCF). CFO indicated mid-teens total revenue growth through 2030 from subscriber growth, pricing, and ad acceleration. Gross margin target 35-40% by 2030. AI Remix licensing agreements signed with UMG, Believe, Kobalt; Q1 2027 launch pending artist opt-ins. LYV partnership 'Reserve by Spotify' expanding to Europe and Australia in 2027.

bullets.title: CCL/RCL: UBS cruise channel check shows strong pricing; Norwegian lagging peers
bullets.body: UBS cruise channel check shows overall booking volumes at mid-single-digit YoY growth (recovering post-election). Caribbean +5%, Europe +6%, Alaska +7% pricing YoY. CCL Princess and RCL Celebrity outperforming on marketing/premium positioning. Norwegian flat to +1% pricing vs peers +3-7%, using aggressive promotions through wave season. CCL Celebration Key still driving demand; water park delayed to 2030. CCL grew yields faster than RCL last year and guiding higher again. UBS Buy on CCL, $36 PT.

bullets.title: WSM: Q3 beat on EPS but Pottery Barn missed; stock -15% on guidance concerns
bullets.body: Williams-Sonoma reported Q3 EPS of $2.38 (beat $2.19 consensus) but comps of +5.1% missed the ~5.5-6% buyside bar; Pottery Barn comps were +1.8% vs +5.1% prior quarter. FY26 guidance reiterated at 4.7-7.2% revenue growth, 17.8-18.2% operating margin. For the first time, management did not reiterate the 'mid-to-high teens operating margin' long-term language. Citi maintains Neutral, cuts PT to $245.

bullets.title: BE: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $335 (Overweight) on third guidance raise, expanding demand
bullets.body: Bloom Energy raised guidance for the third time this year, with increasing demand from utilities, international, and C&I customers. BMO Capital also upgraded BE to Outperform (PT $230). MS Arcaro maintains Overweight with PT raised to $335. Carbon capture commercialization showing positive signs; continued margin expansion.

bullets.title: DELL/HPE: Upcoming earnings in focus; DELL consensus expects $49.3B revenue (+150% ISG)
bullets.body: DELL reports Tuesday post-close (Nov 24) with consensus expecting $49.3B revenue, $6.62 EPS, and ~$19.8B in AI-optimized servers for Q3. Options imply ~14.6% move. HPE reports Monday post-close with consensus at $14.47B revenue; focus on networking and AI server pricing. JPM favors both DELL and HPE over NTAP and HPQ going into prints, citing strong AI infrastructure demand fundamentals.

bullets.title: AMD: Down 8% on Hunterbrook short report; OpenAI reports 14% PPA improvement on AMD chip design
bullets.body: AMD fell ~8% on a Hunterbrook Capital short report alleging AMD has problematic China server exposure via IEIT Systems' firmware access; AMD denied the claims. Separately, OpenAI announced 14% performance-per-watt (PPA) improvements on AMD's flagship GPU IP achieved in under 5 months via AI-driven SystemVerilog optimization—a positive for AMD's competitive position vs Nvidia.

bullets.title: HOOD: Added to Wolfe Alpha List at 23x 2028 EPS; down 36% QTD seen as overdone
bullets.body: Wolfe added Robinhood to its Alpha List citing compelling valuation at 23x 2028 EPS (low end of 20-60x historical range) with strong fundamentals in core trading, a pipeline of revenue-enhancing products, and regulatory/competitive risks viewed as overblown. October net deposits of $15.1B exceeded ~$13B expectations; Trump Accounts contributed $6.5B.

bullets.title: TLN: Oppenheimer raises PT to $450 on 6GW baseload generation opportunity with hyperscalers
bullets.body: Oppenheimer raised Talen Energy's PT to $450 from $400 following management meetings. TLN has ~6GW of baseload generation available for hyperscaler contracting, with organic opportunities in uprates, batteries, peakers, and powered land. Goldman rates TLN Buy at $502 PT (noting no direct Texas exposure). VST and NRG also Buy-rated with 2027 earnings largely intact despite AI infrastructure policy uncertainty.
